The counter in the hallway has been wrong since the day it was installed, and nobody minds. It reads high by four. Visitors who notice are told the story, which takes about a minute and is the best part of the tour. The number itself has never been used for anything.

We tried replacing it twice. The first replacement arrived broken, in a box that had clearly been dropped, and went back the same afternoon. The second worked perfectly and read the same wrong number, which settled the argument about whether the fault was in the counter or in the wiring behind it. Nobody has raised it since.
